rules.title: Node.js image release lines 21 and older are end-of-life
rules.summary: These Node.js release lines no longer receive security or bug fixes, so images tagged with them are built on an unsupported runtime.
rules.replacement: A node image on a supported release line, such as node:22

constraints: Keep the Dockerfile base image, Compose image, CI service containers, and the engines field in package.json on one supported Node.js release line.
Confirm native modules and production dependencies support the target Node.js major.

steps.title: Update the base image
steps.instructions: Change the reported FROM line or Compose image to a tag on a supported release line, and pin it to a digest if your policy requires.

steps.title: Align other image references
steps.instructions: Update other Dockerfiles, Compose files, CI service containers, and deployment manifests that use the same image so they agree.

verification.purpose: Build the image on the new base.
Confirm the container runs the intended Node.js version.

rules.title: Python image release lines 3.10 and older are end-of-life
rules.summary: These Python release lines no longer receive security or bug fixes from the Python core team.
rules.replacement: A python image on a supported release line

constraints: Keep the base image, requires-python, CI matrices, and deployment runtimes on one supported Python release.
Confirm binary wheels and dependencies support the target Python release; rebuild any virtual environment or wheel cache inside the image.

steps.title: Update the base image
steps.instructions: Change the reported FROM line or Compose image to a tag on a supported release line, and pin it to a digest if your policy requires.

steps.title: Align other image references
steps.instructions: Update other Dockerfiles, Compose files, CI service containers, and deployment manifests that use the same image so they agree.

verification.purpose: Build the image on the new base.
Confirm the container runs the intended Python version.

rules.title: PostgreSQL image major versions 13 and older are end-of-life
rules.summary: The PostgreSQL project no longer releases fixes for these major versions.
rules.replacement: A postgres image on a supported major version (the upgrade needs a dump/restore or pg_upgrade)

constraints: A major PostgreSQL upgrade does not reuse the old data directory: the data must be dumped and restored, or migrated with pg_upgrade, before the new image can start on it.
Check extensions, client libraries, and any init scripts against the target major version, and take a backup first.

steps.title: Update the base image
steps.instructions: Change the reported FROM line or Compose image to a tag on a supported release line, and pin it to a digest if your policy requires.

steps.title: Align other image references
steps.instructions: Update other Dockerfiles, Compose files, CI service containers, and deployment manifests that use the same image so they agree.

verification.purpose: Validate the Compose file after changing the image tag.
Confirm the database container runs the intended major version (service name may differ).

rules.title: MySQL image release lines 8.0 and older are past end-of-life
rules.summary: Oracle lists MySQL 8.0 and 5.7 as covered only by Sustaining Support, which means no new fixes.
rules.replacement: A mysql image on a supported release such as the 8.4 LTS line

constraints: A new MySQL release line can need a data directory upgrade; read the upgrade notes and take a backup before starting the new image on existing data.
Check SQL modes, authentication plugins, and client libraries against the target release.

Confirm the database container runs the intended release (service name may differ).

rules.title: Ruby image release lines 3.2 and older are end-of-life
rules.summary: These Ruby branches no longer receive security or bug fixes.
rules.replacement: A ruby image on a supported branch

constraints: Keep the base image, .ruby-version, Gemfile ruby requirement, and CI matrices on one supported Ruby branch.
Confirm gems with native extensions build on the target Ruby, and rebuild bundled gems inside the image.
